selected_problem: Fresh canonical-main inspection found that WorkspaceService.stat followed an existing in-workspace symlink with fs.statSync and reported the referent as a regular file. ChangesetStore.stage therefore accepted the symlink target and snapshotted only referent bytes. A later write atomically renamed a new regular file over the symlink path, while rollback could only restore the captured bytes as another regular file, permanently losing the original symlink identity despite the reversible-delivery contract.

decision_provenance.mode_route_basis: The defect is singular, central to rollbackable self-modification, directly reproduced, and evidence-rich; the committed four-mode router's narrow-bottleneck gate routes DEEP_DEVELOPMENT rather than forcing mode rotation.
decision_provenance.claim_limit: No hosted DWAC success receipt is claimed. The committed DWAC North Star and four-mode router source contracts were replayed against fresh canonical code evidence after the hosted Developer Execution Runtime remained transiently unavailable.

pre_fix_reproduction.scenario: create target.txt and an in-workspace link.txt symlink to it, then stage a write to link.txt
pre_fix_reproduction.expected: UNSUPPORTED_CHANGE_TARGET:link.txt before a changeset document is persisted
pre_fix_reproduction.observed_on_canonical_base: the stage call succeeded because fs.statSync followed the symlink and classified its referent as a regular file

changes: WorkspaceService.stat now uses lstat identity for an existing target before content hashing.
Existing symlinks are surfaced as type=symlink with no referent-content hash, so the existing ChangesetStore.stage non-file target gate rejects them before persistence.
Regular-file hashing, directory rejection, canonical paths, preimage checks, apply/rollback preflight and workspace symlink-escape protection remain intact.
The regression test skips only when the host cannot create a symlink due to platform permissions; on the validation host it executed and passed.
truth_boundaries: This closes the existing in-workspace symlink identity-loss case by rejecting that unsupported transactional target. It does not add symlink-preserving mutation or rollback semantics.
Arbitrary complex repository semantic synthesis remains UNRESOLVED, and filesystem crash-level atomicity for arbitrary I/O/process failure remains unresolved.
No new product form, feature roadmap, provider architecture or hard-coded task-to-mode mapping was introduced.
No GitHub Actions were intentionally triggered or rerun, no force push was used, and no credential, payment, formal Release or destructive/irreversible external action was performed.
